newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: RESEARCH ALERT - Wrightson a sell - Cavill.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT - Wrightson a sell - Cavill.

text.p: Cavill White Securities still rates New Zealand rural services group Wrightson a sell in the short term and recommends remaining underweight in the stock long term, the brokerage firm said in a research document dated March 10.

Earlier this month, Wrightson posted a first half profit of NZ$1.25 million, sharply down from $5.74 million previously, and cut its full year profit forecast to $12-16 million from an adjusted $20-23 million.

"This result highlights the extremely difficult trading conditions prevailing in the New Zealand agricultural sector, due in part to depressed commodity prices," Cavill White's head of research John Cairns said.

"In addition, there is evidence of ongoing decline in demand for a number of core services, wool and livestock broking, and problems in the implementation of the major cost reduction programme heralded last year."

Cavill remained sceptical over the ability of Wrightson to acquire or develop new income streams and said a large part of the company's finance book was inextricably linked to stock and station activities.

"There is considerable risk in the profit forecasts and with high debt levels and the demand for core activities in secular decline, we maintain our recommendation: short term sell, long term underweight," Cavill said.
Cavill forecasts a profit for the full year to June 1997 of NZ$13.0 million, before extraordinary items, for Wrightson.
On Thursday Wrightson shares were trading at NZ$0.94, down two cents. -- Wellington Newsroom (64 4) 4734746
